verdict.rationale: Kitty's first-party docs describe a remote-control facility for driving the terminal from scripts or the shell: opening windows, sending arbitrary text to any window, and changing window and tab titles. A probe confirms an official CLI on the remote-control page, and the ssh kitten forwards remote-control sockets, so a script or agent can drive kitty through a documented public interface. The missing OpenAPI and llms.txt are not material for a desktop terminal's local control API. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of scripted or agent control, and evidence in the pack detailing the underlying wire protocol and full command coverage.
